candidates.name: Polymyalgia Rheumatica
support_spans: elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of proximal muscle weakness, elevated inflammatory markers, and significant weight loss is consistent with Polymyalgia Rheumatica.

candidates.name: Epidural Abscess
support_spans: one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
a single episode of urinary incontinence
contradict_spans: An initial differential of cauda equina syndrome or epidural abscess prompted an urgent MRI of the lumbar spine, which showed mild foraminal narrowing at L5–S1 but no central canal stenosis or abscess
candidates.why: The patient's initial presentation of leg pain, weakness, and urinary incontinence could suggest an epidural abscess, but the MRI results argue against this diagnosis.
